nodes.note: Counting hands and counting observations are separate claims: a solver can obtain the product of binomial coefficients for hands while missing the hidden-mark adjustment or the ordering factor for observations. Split this into hand-count and observation-count nodes.

The hand-side degree and observation-side degree require distinct counting arguments, and a solver can establish either without establishing the other. Split the two degree claims so that an error in counting possible hidden-card completions can be localized separately.

Sorting is not part of the threshold-sum identity; the same partitioned weighted contribution can be established or evaluated without sorting the partner records. Remove sorting from this property and leave sorted-prefix evaluation in accept or in the algorithm node N9.

Requiring balanced groups is an optional implementation choice rather than an essential part of the weighted-query algorithm under these limits. State the algorithm for a partition into two groups, and keep balancing and its 3003-record bound as an implementation example in accept.

The suffix weight recurrence and the weighted-score moment recurrence are separate claims; a solver may compute completion weights without knowing how the additive score affects the first moment. Split the weight computation from the moment computation.

Saturated suffix aggregation needs only total weight, whereas linear suffix aggregation needs the first weighted moment, and a solver can establish or implement one rule without the other. Split the saturated and linear aggregation claims.

Preserving completion values by capping scores and preserving them by merging equal states are distinct invariants; a solver can cap partial records without recognizing the sufficient state for merging. Separate the capping lemma from the weight-merging claim, or incorporate the latter into N15.
